takeaways: [Global Economy] The US Producer Price Index remained flat month-on-month while rising 4.7% annually in July, falling short of projections and signaling a potential cooling in inflationary pressures.

[Equity Markets] The current AI investment cycle is increasingly characterized by a circular flow of capital, where tech giants like Amazon and Alphabet reinvest massive profits back into their own infrastructure and AI services.

[China Economy] China's current account surplus is expanding due to a persistent trade imbalance, where strong export competitiveness and excess industrial capacity are coupled with weak domestic demand that suppresses import growth.
day_verdict: Major day — market-moving events; read carefully.

items.title: Global markets buoyed by US inflation data, Mideast woes linger
bullets: The US Producer Price Index remained flat month-on-month while rising 4.7% annually in July, falling short of projections and signaling a potential cooling in inflationary pressures.
Market expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes have shifted toward December, contributing to a decline in the US Dollar Index below 100 and a five-basis-point drop in 10-year Treasury yields.
items.reason: Market-moving shift in US interest rate expectations.

items.title: Nomura sees resilient H2 CY 26 global economy, but warns of US-Iran tensions, El Niño and AI setback
bullets: Nomura forecasts US core PCE inflation at 3.2% for Q4 2026, suggesting that sticky inflation may force the Federal Reserve to eventually accelerate rate hikes despite current market optimism.

The firm identifies significant downside risks for the second half of the year, specifically citing geopolitical instability in the Middle East, potential El Niño weather impacts, and a possible reversal in AI-driven investment.
items.reason: Comprehensive institutional outlook on macroeconomic risks.

items.title: Are Central Bank Digital Currencies Losing the Race Before It Begins?
bullets: The BIS reports that while 91% of central banks are exploring CBDCs, the focus has shifted toward wholesale applications as private stablecoins—now boasting a $320 billion market cap—gain significant traction in retail payments.

The landscape is fragmenting as major economies diverge: the US is prioritizing regulated private stablecoins, while the Eurozone targets a 2029 launch for a digital euro, creating uncertainty for future financial infrastructure.
items.reason: Structural shift in global payment infrastructure.

items.title: Amazon and Alphabet’s Profits Reveal Circular Nature of A.I. Boom
bullets: The current AI investment cycle is increasingly characterized by a circular flow of capital, where tech giants like Amazon and Alphabet reinvest massive profits back into their own infrastructure and AI services.

This self-reinforcing loop raises questions about the long-term sustainability of AI-driven growth, as the industry's valuation becomes heavily dependent on internal spending rather than external enterprise demand.
items.reason: Highlights a critical structural risk in the current AI-led market rally.

items.title: Alto Ingredients, Inc. ALTO delivered a significantly improved second-quarter 2026 performance
bullets: Despite reporting a strong Q2 with net sales of $245.7 million and a return to profitability, Alto Ingredients shares have plummeted 17% since the earnings release on August 5.

The disconnect between fundamental improvement—driven by higher ethanol crush margins and increased sales volumes—and the stock's underperformance suggests a potential market repricing of the renewable fuels sector.
items.reason: Illustrates a significant earnings-price divergence in the industrial sector.

items.title: Why ‘Canada is not immune’ to the effects of Japan’s surging bond yields
bullets: Rising Japanese government bond yields are incentivizing domestic investors to repatriate capital, potentially reducing demand for U.S. Treasuries and increasing the term premium on long-term debt.

The correlation between U.S. and Canadian bond markets remains high, with approximately 70% to 80% of U.S. yield movements typically translating into the Canadian market, impacting mortgage costs and asset valuations.
items.reason: Highlights a structural shift in global capital flows impacting major sovereign bond markets.

items.title: When will mortgage rates go down from close to a one-year high?
bullets: Despite the Federal Reserve holding rates steady, mortgage rates remain near one-year highs, with the 30-year fixed rate at 6.67% as of mid-August 2026.

Fannie Mae projections suggest mortgage rates will remain elevated in the 6.2% to 6.3% range through 2027, signaling that the housing market may face prolonged pressure from the current interest rate environment.
items.reason: Provides concrete data on consumer-facing interest rates and long-term housing market outlooks.

items.title: China’s Economy Presses Forward Despite Headwinds
bullets: China reported a 4.7% GDP growth rate for the first half of 2026, keeping the country on track to meet its full-year target range of 4.5% to 5% despite a second-quarter slowdown to 4.3%.

High-tech manufacturing and the digital economy now account for nearly 50% of total growth, signaling a successful transition toward new quality productive forces as the country navigates real estate and infrastructure adjustments.
items.reason: Provides critical macroeconomic performance data and structural growth insights.

items.title: China Widening C/A Surplus
bullets: China's current account surplus is expanding due to a persistent trade imbalance, where strong export competitiveness and excess industrial capacity are coupled with weak domestic demand that suppresses import growth.

Analysts project a slow appreciation of the Yuan to 6.65 USDCNY by end-2026 and 6.50 by end-2027, noting that authorities are likely to resist rapid currency shifts to protect export competitiveness against potential 20% tariff hikes.
items.reason: Highlights significant trade imbalances and currency risks impacting global markets.

items.title: CK Asset Nearly Triples Property Sales to $2.8B as Development Profit Falls 57%
bullets: CK Asset reported a 193% surge in property sales revenue to HK$21.6 billion, yet development profit contribution plummeted 57% to HK$765 million, reflecting a sharp margin compression from 24% to 3.5%.

The developer recorded significant impairment charges, including HK$6 billion against its stake in Hui Xian REIT and HK$1.5 billion in investment property value declines, highlighting ongoing valuation pressures in the Hong Kong commercial real estate sector.
items.reason: Significant earnings report from a major developer revealing margin compression and asset impairments.

items.title: URA posts HK$338 million operating surplus after three years of losses
bullets: The Urban Renewal Authority (URA) returned to an operating surplus of HK$338 million in the 2025-26 financial year, ending a three-year streak of losses that previously forced the body to raise HK$8 billion via bond issuance.

Despite the return to profit, the authority remains focused on capital-intensive urban redevelopment and is preparing to launch an enhanced 'Smart Tender' scheme to support property owners in managing engineering costs.
items.reason: Signals a stabilization in the financial health of a key public entity involved in Hong Kong's property development cycle.

items.title: Tech layoffs 2026: Tracking all of the job losses across TikTok, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle, Samsung, Zillow and others
bullets: The technology sector has recorded over 175,000 layoffs in 2026, with Oracle alone cutting 21,000 positions, representing 13% of its workforce, as companies pivot resources toward AI deployment.
Rising labor volatility is prompting regulatory intervention, notably in California, where officials are implementing new tools to monitor AI's impact on employment and labor market stability.
items.reason: Significant labor market shifts driven by AI capital reallocation.

items.title: How Big Tech’s Earnings Are Inflated by Other Tech Companies
bullets: Inter-company spending within the technology sector is creating a circular revenue loop, where major cloud providers report inflated earnings driven by capital expenditures from their own AI-focused client base.

Investors face increased risk as the sustainability of current growth metrics is questioned, given that a significant portion of Big Tech revenue is derived from the reinvestment of venture capital into their own platforms.
items.reason: Fundamental concerns regarding the quality and sustainability of Big Tech earnings.

items.title: OpenAI talent exodus raises 'huge red flag' ahead of IPO
bullets: The departure of key executives, including the chief revenue officer and operating chief, creates significant leadership instability as the company attempts to justify an $852 billion valuation ahead of its IPO.

Market observers view the high-level turnover as a major risk factor, particularly as the firm faces intensifying competition from Google and Anthropic alongside concerns regarding the viability of its long-term business model.
items.reason: Critical leadership instability ahead of a massive IPO.

items.title: Not Micron, Not Sandisk. This Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory Stock Could Be the Next Nvidia.
bullets: SK Hynix has captured a dominant 58% market share in the high-bandwidth memory (HBM) sector, effectively positioning itself as a primary beneficiary of the ongoing shift in AI infrastructure demand toward memory-intensive architectures.

While historically overlooked by Western investors due to its South Korean listing, the company's significant lead over competitors like Micron and Samsung in HBM market share suggests a potential re-rating as its dominance translates into sustained financial momentum.
items.reason: Identifies a dominant market player in a critical AI supply chain bottleneck.

items.title: Goldman in talks with investors on Nvidia financing deal after landing prized role, sources say
bullets: Goldman Sachs is actively courting institutional investors to participate in a massive $500 billion financing initiative designed to sustain the ongoing AI infrastructure boom.

This complex financial structure aims to provide the necessary capital for continued semiconductor expansion, though critics have labeled the aggressive push as a potential 'Wall Street stunt' to maintain market momentum.
items.reason: Significant systemic financial engineering to support AI capital expenditure.

items.title: Cathie Wood's ARK Invest Buys $28M Of Nvidia Rival Cerebras Amid Earnings Selloff
bullets: ARK Invest deployed $28 million to acquire shares of Cerebras, a direct competitor to Nvidia, following a sharp selloff in the rival's stock price after its recent earnings report.

This move highlights a strategic diversification effort by high-profile growth investors looking for alternative semiconductor plays that could challenge Nvidia's current dominance in the AI hardware space.
items.reason: Notable capital rotation by a major institutional investor into the competitive landscape.

items.title: Government could slash EV sales targets as zero emissions mandate comes under review
bullets: The UK government has launched a formal consultation to potentially reduce the 2030 zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) sales target from 80% to as low as 50%, citing industry pressure and difficult global trading conditions.

While the 2035 deadline for a total phase-out of petrol and diesel car sales remains unchanged, the proposed flexibility could allow manufacturers to count more hybrid vehicles toward their annual compliance obligations.
items.reason: Significant regulatory shift impacting major automotive manufacturers' compliance costs and product strategies.

items.title: Global EV Sales Surge: July Hits 1.85M Units, Up 9% - Investing News Network
bullets: Global EV sales reached 1.85 million units in July 2026, a 9% year-on-year increase, though regional performance diverged sharply with a 33% surge in Europe contrasted by a 27% contraction in North America.

The North American decline follows the expiration of federal tax incentives, while China's domestic market continues to stabilize after a difficult start to the year, with manufacturers increasingly pivoting toward aggressive overseas exports.
items.reason: Highlights critical regional market volatility and the impact of subsidy policy changes on global EV demand.

bullets: As Nvidia partners with Wall Street firms to mobilize more than $500 billion of third-party capital for AI infrastructure, the increasingly complex financing underpinning the boom is coming under closer scrutiny....

items.title: Rocket Lab Enters Europe’s Crowded Launch Market
bullets: Rocket Lab has established a German subsidiary to scale satellite production and launch services, directly challenging European incumbents with a significantly higher launch cadence and a $2.13 billion cash reserve.

The move signals an impending price war in the European commercial launch market, as Rocket Lab’s operational maturity and financial resources threaten to outpace local startups currently reliant on limited ESA funding.
items.reason: Significant competitive disruption in the European aerospace market.

items.title: US Space Force gives Rocket Lab $397 million to build threat-tracking 'Flatellites'
bullets: Rocket Lab secured a $397 million contract to develop 'Flatellites' for the Space Force’s SB-AMTI program, marking its largest national defense contract of the year and highlighting its growing role in orbital missile defense.

The company has now accumulated $943 million in U.S. government defense contracts in 2026 alone, underscoring a strategic pivot toward high-margin national security work and mobile, responsive launch capabilities.
items.reason: Major contract win significantly bolsters revenue and government partnership status.
